rows: Consistent with Q2 and full-year profile
Record Q3: revenue ~$385M (+104%); net income $70.5M / $0.89 EPS vs a prior-year $186.5M loss driven by distributor termination expenses.
Record adjusted EBITDA ~$104M (+318%, ~27% of sales) on 860 bps gross margin expansion plus S&M and G&A leverage.
Gross margin expansion driven by lower package/raw-material costs, improved waste, and ~100 bps freight-lane efficiency.
A Q3 promotional allowance accrual adjustment drove a positive margin benefit; excluding it, gross margin would have been consistent with Q2.
Roughly $20M of the Q2-to-Q3 sequential revenue increase came from inventory build, promo allowance adjustments, and SKU/channel mix.
Celsius distribution points are roughly 50% of Monster/Red Bull; long-term goal is to match peer distribution points.
Now the #1 best-selling energy drink on Amazon (21.4% share, ahead of Monster's 18.6% and Red Bull's 13%) and #1 on Instacart.
MULOC energy share reached a record 10.5% - more than doubling year-ago, a level not achieved in the energy category in a decade.
Most successful NACS in company history; 7-Eleven took four Celsius Essentials SKUs chain-wide with gas-pump signage.
Expansion into non-tracked foodservice/independent channels structurally lowers the blended promotional-allowance rate (Monster-like trajectory).
Foodservice expansion: Jersey Mike's national rollout (~2,000 locations, three flavors) and Dunkin' authorization in 3,000-4,000 locations (one SKU).
Celsius Essentials 16oz performance-energy line (270mg caffeine, four flavors) launched at 7-Eleven; nationwide rollout planned 2024, designed to be incremental.
Front-checkout/perfect-store cooler initiative a key win - recent Publix front-end authorization; chain-wide front-checkout placement can unlock 1,000-3,000 stores per chain.
Management flagged a Q4 seasonal pullback at traditional seasonality levels, possibly compounded by a PepsiCo distributor inventory reduction (a PepsiCo decision, 'no guarantees').
Canada is the first major international market under PepsiCo, launching Q1 2024; 2024 build/impact 'inconsequential,' phased through Q1.
International blueprint: target the largest energy markets (UK, Germany, Japan, Australia); using Monster's international structures/P&Ls as a guideline.
2024 innovation pipeline: new core fruit-forward flavors, new Vibe flavors (Cosmic Vibe 'trilogy'), and Vibe flavors extending into the powder/On-The-Go portfolio.
200+ employees added in Q3; drill-deep markets expanding from 23 to over 30 in 2024.
Three-for-one forward stock split effective November 15, 2023.
Household penetration more than doubled to ~25% (from 11.1%); Celsius made the top 10 in total LRB beverages in Q3.
Management tone highly confident and growth-oriented.
Benchmark on where distribution points can go (Celsius ~50% of Monster/Red Bull, convenience ~20% below Bang's peak), and what drove the slower sequential growth in Amazon and Costco vs Q2.

Long-term goal to match Monster/Red Bull's maximum distribution points; still early growth phase, opportunities evolving through 2024 resets; most successful NACS ever. Amazon/Costco slowdown was channel 'lumpiness' - a Prime build in Q2 for Amazon, load-in timing/seasonality for club - while Amazon still gained over 200 bps of share (18.6% to 21.4%); club remains strong with pack-size opportunity.
PepsiCo inventory levels & gross margin sustainability
What to expect for PepsiCo inventory levels in a low-seasonality Q4; and whether two strong quarters change the medium-term 'mid-to-high 40s' gross margin outlook.

Any Q4/Q1 inventory management is PepsiCo's decision with 'no guarantees.' Raw material savings have been consistent and should remain steady into 2024; outbound freight has held but could fluctuate with fuel; operations did an excellent job on scrap/waste/aged inventory and freight lanes - unsure how much more can be squeezed, but in great shape into 2024.
Update on conversations with key retailers around 2024 shelf resets; and where the back-half-weighted 2023 headcount expansion stood in Q3.

Retailers still defining 2024 sets; most successful NACS ever (7-Eleven took four Essentials SKUs chain-wide). 2024 is the first full year of strategic AOP prioritization (2023 joined PepsiCo late in Q4 2022); expanded distribution should appear in IRI scan data around March-April 2024. 2024 budgets call for continued hiring across HR, finance, logistics, ops, sales, marketing; drill-deep markets expand from 23 to over 30.
Unpack the margin drivers - management had guided to a sequential EBITDA margin dip from higher promo/marketing spend, but margins rose - and separate sustainable from one-time factors.

Expansion into foodservice/independent channels carries a lower promotional-allowance profile, plus quarter timing. G&A showed good leverage (YTD ~7.9%), FY2024 expected 7-8% (international build gives some back). S&M averaged ~19-20% this year vs a historical ~22-24%; continued investment in 2024. Gross profit aided by commodity improvement, international cans rolling off the system by Q2, and ~100 bps better freight (~4.9% YTD vs 5.9%).

Whether Canada pipeline fill lands in Q4 or Q1 and any Q4 impact; and how management evaluates international opportunities, alignment with PepsiCo, and the margin impact.

Canada 2024 build/impact 'inconsequential' - good growth/share expected with seeding investment, but not a big inventory/growth driver in Q4 or Q1, rollout phased through Q1. International evaluation targets the largest energy markets (UK, Germany, Japan, Australia); PepsiCo partnerships the priority but other partners possible; too early to detail structures, using Monster's international P&Ls as a guideline.
Components of the ~$20M Q2-to-Q3 sequential benefit
Run through the ~$20M benefit to Q3 revenue - how much was promotional allowance vs inventory built ahead of what was lapped a year ago.

Both Q3 2022 and Q3 2023 had a distributor pipe fill (2023 ~$10-15M), so inventory was not significant to the YoY growth percentage on an apples-to-apples basis; but it was a benefit on the Q2-to-Q3 sequential comparison. Promo-line leverage driven by significant ACV growth and movement into non-tracked channels with shallower promotion; updated promo allowance estimates produced a benefit, keeping the promo % of gross revenue roughly consistent YoY.
Foodservice rollout (Jersey Mike's, Dunkin') & Celsius Essentials differentiation

Timing of the 3,000+ Dunkin' authorization and further eatery rollout; how Celsius Essentials is differentiated and whether it is key to 2024 shelf space; and progress on Celsius branded cooler placement vs the 2023 target.

Foodservice a huge opportunity; Jersey Mike's (~2,000 locations, three flavors) is the first nationwide fast-casual proof-of-concept, ~four weeks in with positive early feedback. Dunkin' authorization covers 3,000-4,000 locations with one SKU. Celsius Essentials limited to particular retailers initially (core/Vibe is priority #1), targets performance-energy, designed to be incremental on top of expected 2024 gains. 2023 cooler goal ~15,000 (working toward it); biggest current win is chain-wide front-checkout cooler authorization (recent Publix front-end win).
Q4 promotional allowances, holiday spend & velocity scope
Whether promotional allowances see material changes in Q4 vs post-adjustment Q3; and the scope for velocity growth over the next 12-24 months given rapid distribution expansion.

For Q4 promos, look to the year-to-date percentage. Q4 S&M trickier with holiday programs; the company plans to keep spending into the holiday season and buyer-reset window to build 2024 velocities. Velocity scope is 'somewhat an unknown' - Celsius is in uncharted territory north of a 10 share; household penetration more than doubled to ~25% (from 11.1%); reset-driven shelf-space expansion should build the billboard effect.
Foodservice source of volume & cross-category merchandising

Whether foodservice consumers are switching from CSDs/teas to Celsius and whether that tracks into retail switches; and whether Celsius could be merchandised outside the energy category throughout the store.

A 'huge unlock' the company is working on but needs more data; the Celsius consumer is incremental with a bigger basket ring (buying Celsius with water/food/snack). Hypothesis that foodservice delivery-app consumers skip the fountain - Celsius is incremental, not competing with the fountain. Already placed in grab-and-go sections at some stores (Ralphs, Publix, Kroger), opening a bigger TAM; Celsius made the top 10 in total LRB beverages.
How management is thinking about Q4 seasonality given the comparison to last year's Pepsi launch; and whether there is substantial 2024 innovation beyond Celsius Essentials.

Category seasonality is real - anticipate a Q4 pullback at traditional seasonality levels, possibly compounded by a PepsiCo distributor inventory reduction. Beyond Celsius Essentials, 2024 innovation includes new core fruit-forward flavors, new Vibe flavors (Cosmic Vibe 'trilogy'), and expansion of the powder/On-The-Go portfolio with Vibe flavors - driven by growing retailer interest.
